submitted.summary: Conjecture 3.33 is false at (r,d) = (2,5): no integer- (indeed real-) valued submodular function on {0,1}^16 is negative exactly on the degree-2 monomial image of {0,1}^5.
submitted.body:
At degree two in five variables, the monomial map has 16 output coordinates, including the empty-product coordinate. A four-edge dependency cycle gives the obstruction; an independent thirteen-row symmetric certificate is the argument formalized in Lean. The result rules out even a real-valued submodular separator, without any efficient-evaluation requirement. The claim concerns the read 2019 preprints; retention in the unread 2022 journal version is not asserted.

**Result and scope:** Conjecture 3.33 is false at (r,d) = (2,5): no integer- (indeed real-) valued submodular function on {0,1}^16 is negative exactly on the degree-2 monomial image of {0,1}^5.

**Complete proof and verification sources:** [A four-edge obstruction to submodular separation of quadratic Boolean monomial images: a counterexample to Brakensiek-Gopi-Guruswami Conjecture 3.33 (arXiv:1902.04740; ECCC TR19-013)](https://mathdb.com/abs/2611.00053) · [PDF](https://mathdb.com/pdf/2611.00053v1).

The paper page includes the supplementary proof-source JSON attachment and `extract_sources.py`, which reconstruct the archived proof and verification sources. The linked paper gives the complete rigorous argument and specifies exactly which statements are formalized.

This is an AI-assisted research preprint. Internal review is not external journal peer review; bounded prior-art searches do not certify worldwide priority. See the paper for the source, interpretation, formalization, and trust limitations.
